latest_lesson.topic_title: Navigating the First Week at a New Job
latest_lesson.article: Starting a new job is always a whirlwind of emotions. Last Monday, I walked into the office feeling like a fish out of water. Not only did I struggle to remember everyone's name, but I also felt overwhelmed by the endless stream of emails. My manager, Sarah, noticed my hesitation and suggested, 'If you were to have any questions, don't hesitate to reach out.' That really broke the ice. By Wednesday, I started getting the hang of the workflow. I’ve realized that being proactive is key here. Instead of waiting for tasks, I try to touch base with my teammates to see how I can pitch in. It is not just about the technical skills; it is about building rapport. Had I known how supportive the team would be, I wouldn't have been so nervous. Now, I am finally settling into the groove. Whether you are a fresh graduate or a seasoned pro, the first week is rarely a walk in the park, but it is definitely a vital step toward professional growth. Just keep your chin up and stay curious!

vocabulary.meaning_zh: 感到渾身不自在的人（像離水的魚）
vocabulary.example: I felt like a fish out of water at the formal gala since I didn't know anyone.
A funny joke is a great way to break the ice during a first meeting.
Let's touch base next week to discuss the project update.
If everyone pitches in, we can finish this report by five o'clock.
Learning to use the new software was a walk in the park for him.

podcast_script.speaker: Alex
podcast_script.text: Hey Maya, I just finished reading this article about surviving your first week at a new job. It sounds so familiar, doesn't it?

podcast_script.speaker: Maya
podcast_script.text: Oh, totally! I remember feeling like a fish out of water when I started my first internship. It was super nerve-wracking.

podcast_script.speaker: Alex
podcast_script.text: Exactly. The author mentioned, 'If you were to have any questions, don't hesitate to reach out.' That’s a classic, polite way to ease someone's anxiety.

podcast_script.speaker: Maya
podcast_script.text: Right, and using those conditional sentences makes it sound so professional yet approachable. Did you find it easy to break the ice with your team?

podcast_script.speaker: Alex
podcast_script.text: Not really. I’m quite shy, so I usually just wait for people to talk to me. But the article says it’s better to be proactive.

podcast_script.speaker: Maya
podcast_script.text: I agree. You really have to touch base with your colleagues if you want to be part of the loop. Like, just ask if you can pitch in on something.

podcast_script.speaker: Alex
podcast_script.text: That’s a good point. 'Had I known that earlier,' I would have been much more confident in my previous role.

podcast_script.speaker: Maya
podcast_script.text: See? You’re already using those advanced structures! Honestly, starting a new job is never a walk in the park, but you’ll get there.

comprehension_quiz.question: Which of the following best describes the author's feeling at the beginning of the new job?
comprehension_quiz.explanation_zh: 文中提到作者剛到職時覺得自己像「離水的魚」（a fish out of water），且感到不知所措（overwhelmed），故選 1。

comprehension_quiz.question: Choose the correct grammatical form to complete the sentence: '____ I known about the meeting, I would have prepared the slides.'
comprehension_quiz.explanation_zh: 這是過去與事實相反的假設語氣倒裝句（Inversion），原本是 If I had known...，倒裝後將 Had 移至句首，故選 1。
